reviews.summary: 11 findings (3 medium, 8 low). The worst: in context-window, the Checkpoint continue-first and the Final test question spot-compact-before-qa test the same rule (the next Phase fits, so carry on) with the same three distractors, so the Final test checks recognition instead of transfer. Lint passes on all four Lessons. Every Site story claim and every direct quote checked out against the repo, the transcripts or the cited page. All the /learn links point at the right Lessons, and no Lesson contradicts the course facts.

findings.where: context-window, "At a Phase boundary: Matt's order", Checkpoint continue-first (lines 179-189), against Final test spot-compact-before-qa (lines 420-430)
findings.problem: The Checkpoint and the Final test question test the same idea: at a boundary, question 1 says yes, so carry on. They also share three of their four options: compact, clear and handoff are wrong, and carry on is right. A reader who did the Checkpoint can answer the Final test by spotting the pattern. This breaks the writing guide's "Don't reuse a Checkpoint as a Final test question" and the pilot rule that "no Checkpoint duplicates a Final test question".
findings.evidence: Checkpoint (line 180): "You've finished grilling a small change ... at about 35k tokens. Next you'll build it ... What does Matt's tree say?" Options: "`/compact`, since it's the default" / "`/clear`, since the decisions are made" / "`/handoff`, so the build starts from a clean brief" / [x] "Carry on, since the build needs the grilling". Final test (line 421): "Ana finishes building a search box at 60k tokens. Next she'll check it by hand ... She types `/compact` first". Options: "`/clear` instead" / "compacted mid-build" / "`/handoff` instead" / [x] "carry on in this session". Writing guide, Questions section, and "Lessons from the pilot review".
findings.fix: Make the Checkpoint test the other rule in its section, the one no Final test question checks: don't decide mid-Phase. For example: "Halfway through building, `/context` shows 110k and the build isn't finished. What now?" Right answer: keep going, or hand the rest to subagents, and decide at the boundary. Wrong answers: `/compact` now, `/clear` now, `/handoff` now. Keep spot-compact-before-qa as the Final test check of question 1.

findings.where: context-window, "`/handoff`: when the work has to travel", Checkpoint handoff-reason option d (lines 237-238), against Final test scenario-afk-review (lines 384-394)
findings.problem: A Checkpoint distractor gives the Final test's scenario and its answer. Option d of handoff-reason is "diff reviewed while you step away", and its feedback says it goes to a subagent. scenario-afk-review then asks about a diff review while you're at lunch, and the answer is a subagent. The body (line 153: "Automated review of the diff ... is the usual case") and Scene step 3 (line 171) already use review as their example, so the Final test checks recognition, not transfer. This breaks the writing guide's rules "Questions test transfer, not recognition" and no Checkpoint duplicating a Final test question. scenario-afk-review came from the stopped round-2 fixer, and no check round ever looked at it (context-window.json: next = round 2 fix, stopped).
findings.evidence: Line 237: "- [ ] You want the diff reviewed while you step away." Line 238: "> A tightly scoped job that needs no steering goes to a subagent." Line 385: "the diff should be checked against the spec, and you'll be at lunch while that runs. Which move does Matt's tree pick?" Line 392: "[x] A subagent, which reports back when done."
findings.fix: Change option d of handoff-reason to a case that isn't a handoff and doesn't involve a subagent, for example "The next task is an unrelated bug in another part of the site", with feedback saying `/clear` is cheaper. Alternatively, give scenario-afk-review an AFK task that isn't a review, such as translating 30 error messages using an existing glossary while you're at lunch, so the reader has to apply question 4 to a new kind of job.

findings.fix: Gloss each term where it first appears. Line 55: "(kept free so Claude Code can compact, or summarise, the conversation; see below)". Line 81: "many turns (a message and everything the agent does in reply) ago". Line 199: "decision records (notes on why a hard-to-undo choice was made), commits (saved snapshots of the code in Git)".

findings.problem: Implement and The main flow tell you to run the full-name review in the same session that did the building, and say the fresh sub-agents make that safe. Code review teaches the opposite: the sub-agents start fresh anyway, but the agent writing their briefs and passing on their reports still carries the build's assumptions, so you review from a clean session. Its Final test marks reviewing in the build session as the mistake. A reader of all three Lessons gets two rules, and the Implement Scene (a worked example) shows the practice Code review warns against. This came from a round-1 implement fix ('which code-review's fresh sub-agents avoid'). Code review's reasoning was corrected after that, so the fix is now out of date. It was never declined.
